details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:lines 91-98 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `\bneeds?\s+GitHub\s+writes?\b` pattern can treat descriptive text mentioning a need for GitHub writes as a permission request.
  WHY: This can consume the stop-block budget on non-asking text; the source rates this NIT.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:Line: 355 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The inline-question regex matches only two choices, so it misses questions with three or more choices.
  WHY: An unattended session can end its turn on a three-choice question without being blocked; the source rates this MAJOR.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:147-387 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The `read_blocks`/`write_blocks` stop-counter update is not atomic, so overlapping hook invocations can lose an increment.
  WHY: A lost increment can delay the stop-block cap; severity disagreement: Google rated this MAJOR, while DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Grok rated it NIT.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:177-221 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `load_transcript` reads and parses the full transcript on a Stop event, and `current_turn` iterates it to find the current turn.
  WHY: For long sessions this can consume unnecessary time and risk exceeding the 30-second hook timeout; severity disagreement: Google rated this MAJOR, while DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Grok rated it NIT.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:Line: 99 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Truncating the sanitized session ID to 120 characters for the marker filename can cause distinct session IDs with the same prefix to share a marker path.
  WHY: A collision can overwrite a marker and leave the originally marked session without its guard; the sources rate this NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Implement unattended question guard enforced in issue mode sessions.
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The logic correctly blocks but does not seem to fulfill the intent of notifying the user via the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment when the `STOP_BLOCK_CAP` is reached; it just logs to a local file, which may be unreachable by the operator during unattended issue-mode.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 91-98, `_PERMISSION_ASK_RES` pattern `\bneeds?\s+GitHub writes?\b` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The regex can trigger on descriptive text mentioning GitHub writes, rather than only on a request for permissions.
  WHY: A false-positive block consumes the stop-block budget on non-asking text.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: `read_blocks` (line 152) followed by `write_blocks` (line 387) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The stop-block counter uses a read-modify-write sequence without an atomicity guard.
  WHY: Concurrent Stop events could lose an increment, though the source says hook invocation is serial per session and considers the race unlikely.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: `load_transcript` (line 186) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `load_transcript` reads the entire transcript JSONL file before `current_turn` filters to the last turn.
  WHY: Long sessions could increase time and memory use, though the source considers exceeding the 30-second timeout unlikely.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:Line: 355 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The inline-question regex matches exactly two choices and misses questions with three choices.
  WHY: The guard will not block an unattended session ending its turn on a 3-choice inline question, violating CLAUDE.md §28.G.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:Line: 147-167 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `read_blocks` followed by `write_blocks` sequence is not atomic.
  WHY: Two concurrent hook invocations can both read the same `stop_blocks` value and write back the same incremented value, causing the guard to under-count blocks and potentially exceed the `STOP_BLOCK_CAP` without escalation.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:Line: 177-190 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `load_transcript` reads the entire transcript file line-by-line in every `Stop` event.
  WHY: For very long sessions, this could cause the hook to exceed its 30-second execution timeout configured in `settings.json`, leading to unpredictable behavior or hook failures.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:Line: 99 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Session ID is truncated to 120 characters in the file stem.
  WHY: This truncation creates a fragile invariant that could lead to collisions or errors if future logic relies solely on the stem filename without strictly re-validating the full ID from the file content.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Implement unattended question guard enforced in issue mode sessions.
  Expected change site: .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py
  Evidence of absence: The logic correctly blocks but does not seem to fulfill the intent of notifying the user via the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment when the `STOP_BLOCK_CAP` is reached; it just logs to a local file, which may be unreachable by the operator during unattended issue-mode.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: `evaluate()` — read_blocks (line ~184) followed by write_blocks (line ~196) in the stop path | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The read-then-write sequence is not atomic.
  WHY: Overlapping Stop events could both read `blocks=0`, write `blocks=1`, and trip the cap one block later than intended, though the source says hooks generally run serially per session.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: load_transcript (line ~177) and current_turn (line ~221) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `load_transcript` reads and parses the entire transcript, then `current_turn` iterates it to find the last user prompt.
  WHY: Long sessions could push this O(n) work past the 30-second hook timeout.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: _stem (line ~99) and marker_path (line ~103) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_stem` truncates the sanitized session ID to 120 characters before using it as the marker filename.
  WHY: Two distinct session IDs sharing the first 120 characters could collide, overwrite a marker, and leave the originally marked session unprotected.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  PROBLEM: The stop_blocks counter update is non-atomic.
  WHY: Concurrent hook invocations could both read the same value and write the same incremented value, losing a block increment.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: load_transcript()~177 (full file read) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `load_transcript()` reads the entire transcript on every Stop when `last_assistant_message` is absent.
  WHY: Long sessions could approach the 30-second `settings.json` timeout before `final_assistant_text()` runs.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: _stem()~99 (120-char truncation) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The session ID is truncated without an explicit comment on collision safety.
  WHY: Future changes that weaken the `read_marker()` session-equality check could cause marker collisions.
